systemPrompt: You are a character-card designer for an NSFW-capable roleplay app. Be vivid, concrete, and in-character. Use {{user}} for the player and {{char}} for the character. Explicit content is allowed when the scene calls for it. Output ONLY the requested field's content — no preamble, no headings, no commentary, no quotation. Do NOT echo the upstream details, the example character, or any tags back; produce new content for the requested field. CRITICAL: when you write content that names the character, use the TARGET CHARACTER's `name` (or {{char}}); never substitute the EXAMPLE CHARACTER's name into the output.

literal.instruction: Write the {humanName} for this character. Be direct and concrete; lean on the upstream details and tags as guidance, but do not repeat them. Aim for {wordCount} words.

creative.instruction: Write the {humanName} for this character with a distinctive sensory or atmospheric hook. Pick a register the example character would NOT have used; surprise the reader. Lean on the tags for genre signals but do not repeat them verbatim. Aim for {wordCount} words.

terse.instruction: Write the {humanName} for this character in TWO short sentences only. No qualifiers, no atmospheric setup, no listing. Give the spine — the author will expand. Strict cap: {wordCount} words.

name.humanName: character's given name ONLY — no occupation, title, age, descriptor, or 'the X' suffix. Just the name (e.g. 'Vexara', 'Gemma', 'Mira Vance'). One or two words.

nickname.humanName: casual short alias (1-3 words). Either a shortening of the full name ('Vex' for 'Vexara', 'Gem' for 'Gemma') OR a non-intimate sensory/visual tag rooted in something specific about the character ('the curly-haired one', 'sparrow', 'redshirt', 'star-eyes'). MUST DIFFER from the full name. Avoid generic terms of endearment ('sweetheart', 'princess', 'darling') unless the character's role / setting genuinely calls for one.

personality.humanName: personality (traits, manner, what catches people off guard)

literal.instruction: Write the first message — the opening line that {{char}} (the TARGET character, NOT the example character) speaks when {{user}} arrives. Third-person past-tense narration in *italics* for actions, plain text for spoken dialogue in quotes. Use the TARGET character's name from the upstream block — NEVER use the example character's name. ~{wordCount} words.

creative.instruction: Write the first message that {{char}} (the TARGET character) speaks when {{user}} arrives. Open on a sensory hook — gesture, image, sound — not on the character's name or role. Third-person past-tense italics for actions, quoted speech for dialogue. Use the TARGET character's name from the upstream block; do NOT use the example character's name. ~{wordCount} words.

terse.instruction: Write a punchy first message for {{char}} (the TARGET character): one short *action line* + one short spoken sentence. Use the TARGET character's name from the upstream block — never the example character's. ≤{wordCount} words.

message_example.humanName: example dialogue (two short exchanges in <START>...{{user}}...{{char}}... format)

literal.instruction: Write example dialogue for {{char}} (the TARGET character). Two short exchanges, each starting with <START>. Format every line as either '{{user}}: ...' or '{{char}}: ...' (literal handlebars — they are placeholders the engine substitutes at runtime). Use the TARGET character's voice; do NOT use the example character's name in the dialogue. ~{wordCount} words.

creative.instruction: Write example dialogue for {{char}} (the TARGET character). Two short exchanges, each starting with <START>. Pick exchanges that surprise — one about a topic the upstream tags don't telegraph. Format every line as either '{{user}}: ...' or '{{char}}: ...'. Do NOT use the example character's name in the dialogue. ~{wordCount} words.

terse.instruction: Write example dialogue for {{char}}: one <START> exchange, two lines (one '{{user}}:' and one '{{char}}:'). Do NOT use the example character's name. ≤{wordCount} words.

literal.instruction: Write an alternate greeting for {{char}} (the TARGET character) — a different opening from the existing first_message but in the same voice. Third-person past-tense italics for actions, quoted speech for dialogue. Use the TARGET character's name from the upstream block — NEVER use the example character's name. ~{wordCount} words.

creative.instruction: Write a distinctive alternate greeting for {{char}} (the TARGET character) — different setting, mood, or tone from the existing first_message. Use the TARGET character's name from the upstream block; do NOT use the example character's name. ~{wordCount} words.

terse.instruction: Write a short alternate greeting for {{char}} (the TARGET character): one *action line* + one spoken sentence. Use the TARGET character's name; never the example character's. ≤{wordCount} words.

literal.instruction: Write a group-chat greeting for {{char}} (the TARGET character) — assumes {{user}} is one of multiple speakers and acknowledges the social context. Use the TARGET character's name from the upstream block — NEVER use the example character's name. ~{wordCount} words.

creative.instruction: Write a distinctive group-chat greeting for {{char}} (the TARGET character) — picks up on a moment between others, or addresses a specific other speaker. Use the TARGET character's name; do NOT use the example character's name. ~{wordCount} words.

terse.instruction: Write a short group-chat greeting for {{char}}: one action + one spoken line that hints at multiple speakers. Use the TARGET character's name; never the example character's. ≤{wordCount} words.

system_prompt.humanName: system prompt (instructions to the model about how to portray {{char}})

post_history_instructions.humanName: post-history instructions (generic stage-direction text only — pure formatting/tone guidance with NO mention of the character's name, traits, profession, or biography. ✅ Good: 'Stay in character. Respond in third person past tense. Keep responses under three paragraphs.' ❌ Bad: 'Maintain Sarah's dry humor and observant eye.' ❌ Bad: 'Channel the warm, professional agency companion tone.' If unsure, output only generic directives that would apply to ANY character)

depth_prompt.humanName: depth prompt (a short note that lives N turns deep in the prompt)

creator_notes.humanName: creator notes (a short note for the player who will use the card — content warnings, NSFW posture, intended audience, edge-case handling. NOT model recommendations and NOT a re-summary of the character)

details_sex.humanName: sex (one of: Male, Female, Non-binary, or a short custom descriptor like 'futa' or 'agender')

details_age.humanName: age — a bare number ('22'), short descriptor ('mid-30s', 'ancient', 'immortal'), or 'unknown'. Do NOT append 'years old', 'yrs', or any qualifier.

details_mood.humanName: mood / disposition (default emotional register, what shifts it)

intimacy_build.humanName: build (body shape, frame, how {{char}} carries themselves)

intimacy_anatomy.humanName: anatomy (concrete, vivid; non-human anatomy described frankly when applicable)

intimacy_markings.humanName: markings (tattoos, scars, piercings, jewelry rarely removed)

intimacy_sensitivities.humanName: sensitivities (places that get a strong reaction)

intimacy_scent.humanName: scent (day/work scent vs. fresh-out-of-bath; intimate scent)

literal.instruction: Write 3-4 specific turn-ons for this character as a bullet list, one '- item' per line. Each item is a short phrase (5-12 words). Lean on the personality and anatomy already given but do not echo them. ~{wordCount} words total.

creative.instruction: Write 3-4 distinctive turn-ons for this character as a bullet list, one '- item' per line. Pick angles the upstream details don't telegraph; surprise the reader. Each item is a short phrase. ~{wordCount} words total.

terse.instruction: Write 3 short turn-ons as a bullet list, one '- item' per line. ≤4 words each. No setup, no qualifiers.

literal.instruction: Write 3-4 specific kinks for this character as a bullet list, one '- item' per line. Each item is a concrete preference (3-10 words). Distinct from broader turn-ons. ~{wordCount} words total.

creative.instruction: Write 3-4 distinctive kinks for this character as a bullet list, one '- item' per line. Pick specifics the upstream tags don't already imply. Each item is a concrete preference. ~{wordCount} words total.

terse.instruction: Write 3 short kinks as a bullet list, one '- item' per line. ≤4 words each.

literal.instruction: Write 3-4 hard nos as a bullet list, one '- item' per line. These are neutral starting-point limits the author should review and edit; not character-specific. Examples: family roles, degradation, scat. ~{wordCount} words total.

creative.instruction: Write 3-4 hard nos as a bullet list, one '- item' per line. Pick reasonable defaults the author can keep or replace. ~{wordCount} words total.

terse.instruction: Write 3 short hard nos as a bullet list, one '- item' per line. ≤4 words each.
